speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with a psychiatric condition and new-onset movement disorder. To begin my evaluation, please tell me what specific symptoms you are experiencing and when they started.

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is good news regarding your psychiatric symptoms. However, I notice you mentioned a "new-onset movement disorder"; can you describe the specific involuntary movements or stiffness you are experiencing since starting risperidone?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your report of inability to remain still, fidgeting, and repetitive leg movements, you are exhibiting signs of acute dystonia or akathisia. Given your recent start on risperidone, these are likely side effects. I need to confirm if these symptoms have started suddenly and if you have any muscle stiffness or pain. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Electrolytes, Renal_Function.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC 5,000 /μL, Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 250,000 /μL; Electrolytes: Sodium 140 mEq/L, Potassium 4.0 mEq/L, Chloride 100 mEq/L, Bicarbonate 24 mEq/L; Renal_Function: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for providing those labs; they are within normal limits, which rules out metabolic causes for your movement symptoms. To confirm the nature of your restlessness and differentiate between akathisia and tardive dyskinesia, could you tell me if you feel an inner urge to move your legs, or if the movements are choreiform and involuntary? Have you noticed any difficulty swallowing or drooling since starting the medication?

REQUEST TEST: Tolerability_of_Antipsychotic_Treatment

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Tolerability_of_Antipsychotic_Treatment: Patient exhibits significant akathisia characterized by inability to remain still, frequent pacing, fidgeting, and repetitive leg movements. Psychiatric symptoms (psychosis) have improved significantly. No signs of acute dystonia (muscle stiffness/pain) or tardive dyskinesia (choreiform involuntary movements) noted. No difficulty swallowing or drooling reported.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Akathisia secondary to Risperidone.
